stage: qualification slice (stage 1), route A: sequential, checkpointed, one core per dataset
declared: 2026-10-02, R052; revision 3 after Codex's launch reviews 523249d (A-H) and e44f804 (R1-R7); PROPOSED - runs only after Codex's review of this revision and the owner's go
purpose: measure the refit chain under the section 7.4 start policy on Lengau - per-resample time, the original fit, peak memory, utilisation - and prove checkpointed recovery across PBS jobs on an exact-index subchain; this slice reads NO coverage (no policy-matched reference exists yet) and produces no scientific row; its status files carry the completed chain's aggregation for the record, which is not read before the slice report

datasets.seed_rule: simulate.dataset_seed(generator, grid, rep, D, seed_base): the three RESOLVED 31-bit seeds are listed in resolved_seeds and are checked by the runner against excluded_resolved_seeds - the resolved seeds of every historical M2S identity at omega 1 and 2, D = 4, reps 0..999, seed_base 2026 and 2027 (the refit probe, d4v12b and the omega-2 bank); the bootstrap index matrix, folds and per-index fit seeds are structural and need not be disjoint from historical runs

cfg.note: B = 200 from the start: a changed B changes the identity, so no short-B timing run contributes; eight cold outer starts, four cold inner starts, plus every member's section 7.4 additions; M2S on its conservative interim (OPEN)

control.rule: the recovery control: dataset rep 0's resample indices 0..19 under the UNCHANGED B = 200 identity, bound by --until 20 on every run (a cumulative target, never a count of new work): C1 normal (--until 20 --kind c1, 48 h serial, no interruption, its own root row19_slice_ctl_normal); C2 interrupted (--until 20 --kind c2 --pbs-kill-control: no cooperative deadline, PBS kills it at walltime W_int, its own root row19_slice_ctl_interrupted); C3 resume (--until 20 --kind c3, 48 h) in C2's root. chpc/row19_control_compare.py rebuilds the frozen task from this manifest and the task binding, validates every record (checksum, identity, seed, B, the identity's own draw per index, every predictor and band finite unless failed with a reason, fit seconds finite), the exact index set 0..19 in both, both statuses bound to the task with typed roles (C1 fresh, C3 resumed), and the interruption record (typed; the C2 job id bound in the campaign ledger; a non-zero PBS exit; walltime used >= requested; 1..19 accepted records before the kill equal to C3's resumed count; the original cache reused; whether a tail fragment was present); parity is reported separately from qualification and a parity of failed resamples qualifies nothing. The control ends at 0..19: no continuation to B = 200 is promised; the main datasets measure full chains
control.W_int_rule: ONE prospective rule: C1 runs FIRST (with the three main datasets); C2 is reserved and submitted only after C1's original fit and its first three resamples have been recorded (status/timing of C1 on Lustre), with W_int = C1's measured original seconds + 3 x the median of those first resamples, rounded up to the minute, and in any case between original + 1 and original + 19 resamples and below 48 h; stage 0 (a same-shaped M3H layer) is a planning proxy for the first-record allowance only, never the W_int source; a C2 killed inside the original, ended cooperatively or completed normally is recorded NON-QUALIFICATION, never a passing control; C1's 48 h must cover its original + 20 refits + start-up and flush, else a legal control endpoint is declared prospectively before C1 is submitted
control.interruption_record: <C2 root>/c2_interruption.json written by the operator from qstat -xf and the checkpoint: job_id, exit_status (int), walltime_requested_s, walltime_used_s, pbs_killed (bool), accepted_records_before (int, from checkpoint_state), original_cache_reused (bool, from C3's status), tail_fragment_present (bool, from checkpoint_state before C3)
control.launch_order: C1 + main rep 0, 1, 2 together on the owner's go; C2 after C1's first records set W_int; C3 after C2's kill; every one through a prior reservation

code.commit: TBD (RSC): the policy at 5f6333c + the refit slice hooks (ff82dd0; until, should_stop, checkpoint_state and analyze_dataset(interval_result=) in this revision) + the runner, the campaign ledger, the comparator and the watch of this revision; the Lustre clone rsc_slice carries them; the pinned file hashes below are the files at that commit
code.policy_config_hash: edcfdf4300f3 (D = 4, layer 41, seed 2026, refit, four inner cold starts; the slice's own hash is recomputed and recorded by the runner)

environment.toolchain: /mnt/lustre/users/pvanrooyen/t1_toolchain (t1py = the pinned wrapper above, t1site, rootfs python:3.12.10-slim-bookworm), clone rsc_slice (dedicated to this slice; never a tree another job uses)
environment.threads: NPROC=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, all set by the runner before any import and verified at admission; no joblib workers (they cannot spawn under the image loader)
environment.identity_rule: the runner refuses (exit 4) when any pinned version, the machine, the backend, a thread cap or the wrapper's hash differs from this manifest; the observed values are recorded in every status file

pbs.note: the runner stops dispatching new resamples 30 minutes before the walltime (not on C2), finishes the resample in flight, flushes and exits 75 for resumption; each submission needs a reservation token from the campaign ledger

templates.control: chpc/row19_slice_control.pbs.template (serial; C1 normal 48 h, C2 interrupted at a short walltime, C3 resume 48 h)

pbs.memory_rule: select=1:ncpus=1:mem=8gb on every job; the runner requests a stop at the next record boundary and exits 4 (HELD) when its ru_maxrss exceeds 6 GiB; PBS kills at 8 GB; row 18 measured about 1 GiB for one full layer
pbs.submission_rule: chpc/row19_ledger.py reserve refuses a fifth reservation for a dataset and any reservation that would breach the cap
pbs.log_rule: each job streams its stdout and stderr through tee to <root>/live_*.log; the PBS script keeps BOTH pipe statuses (the runner's and tee's), writes the terminal 'exit <rc> tee <rc>' line to the PBS output AND to the live log, and exits with the runner's status; a live log without its terminal line is an incomplete observation (the watch alarms), and a tee failure is recorded, never hidden

storage.checkpoints: <root>/ckpt (one fsynced JSONL per dataset identity, exclusive lock per writer)
storage.original_run_cache: <root>/orig (the original run_dataset outputs per dataset identity, so a resume never redoes the original fit)
storage.ledgers: <campaign>/budget.json (the ONE campaign ledger: reservations, bindings, runner wall/exit, settlements), <root>/task_<rep>.json (binding + per-record watermark + runs + recompute authorizations), <root>/task_index.json (rep -> identity, decides fresh versus recovering), <root>/timing_<rep>.jsonl (one line per durable record), <root>/status_<rep>.json, <root>/STOP_ACK_rep<N>.json (names the request id and the boundary)
storage.backup: every poll of chpc/row19_watch.py pulls the campaign ledger and each root's task bindings, status, timing, checkpoint, original-cache and live-log files to RSC chpc/results/row19_slice/live/ (held and interrupted evidence included); Lustre purges files older than 90 days and is not backed up
storage.ledger: <campaign>/budget.json under <campaign>/budget.lock: ONE counter for every root, control and stage 0 (chpc/row19_ledger.py); a reservation is made BEFORE qsub, bound to the PBS job id, marked live by the runner, and settled only from qstat -xf resources_used.walltime x cores; a killed or vanished job keeps its full reservation until settled
storage.task_binding: <root>/task_<rep>.json (manifest sha, rep, resolved seed, identity, B, target, paths) + <root>/task_<rep>.lock (exclusive owner for the whole run)

budget.rule: enforced by chpc/row19_ledger.py: a reservation (cores x walltime of the FILLED PBS request) is refused when spent + live reservations + it exceeds the cap, when the campaign is already over its cap, when the (kind, rep) has its maximum reservations, or when any number is not finite and positive; the runner is admitted only with a reservation bound to its job id that carries its own cores and walltime; a job's reservation stays live until the operator settles it from qstat -xf allocated time (a killed or vanished job keeps its full reservation); settled is terminal; the manifest's cap must equal the ledger's; on exhaustion the run stops and the incomplete report is retained; nothing is reset
budget.envelope: worst case at one core: 24 (stage 0) + 48 (C1) + W_int (C2) + 48 (C3) + 144 N (main charges) <= 1,500, so at most nine full-length main charges for W_int <= 48 h, eight if the second C3 reservation is used at W_int > 36 h; verified settlements free headroom without raising the per-dataset maximum of four submissions

stops.identity: code hashes, environment versions and the dataset identity must equal the manifest's and the checkpoint's, else exit 4 (held)
stops.damage: strict restore: an unacceptable checkpoint record holds the run (exit 4) for diagnosis; only a trailing fragment is repaired
stops.deadline: no new resample after walltime - reserve; exit 75 (resume)
stops.budget: exit 4 before any fit when the cap would be breached
stops.second_writer: exit 4 when the dataset's checkpoint lock is held
stops.memory: ru_maxrss above 6 GiB: diagnosed at admission (held before any original work), before every dispatch (stop at the next record boundary), and after the last record and on no-work restores (a completed chain with a breached peak exits 4, never 0); an in-flight fit finishes under the declared rule - no instantaneous enforcement; PBS kills at the 8 GB request
stops.stop_request: <campaign>/STOP or STOP_rep<N> (each carries a request id): checked BEFORE the original fit (a request present at admission buys nothing: exit 75, acknowledged 'before the original'), before EVERY dispatch, and after the last durable record and on a no-work restore; the acknowledgment names the request id, scope, job and boundary; an old acknowledgment never satisfies a new request
stops.task: a task binding that differs from the one started in the root, a missing binding beside prior evidence for the rep (task index, status, timing, acknowledgment, checkpoint or cache), a rep outside datasets.reps, a resolved seed differing from the declared one, a role/target/kill-mode contract that does not match the kind, a second owner, a checkpoint with rejected or conflicting records, fewer accepted records than the per-record watermark, or a missing/damaged/undecodable original cache beside committed records: exit 4
stops.reservation: no reservation token, or one not bound to this PBS job, kind, rep and root: exit 4 before anything

measurements: per durable record: fit seconds and ru_maxrss at that record (timing_<rep>.jsonl; the record is fsynced first, then the timing line and the watermark)
the original run: wall seconds of run_dataset in this process when computed fresh (jit compilation INCLUDED, NOT separated); the cached value when restored
compilation proxy ONLY: the first new resample's excess over the median new resample of the same job (status first_new_fit_s, median_new_fit_s)
aggregation_seconds: the completed chain's aggregation; publication_seconds: the final status/ACK/task/ledger writes
wall_seconds_main: from main() start to the final publication (imports before main excluded; wrapper and PBS start-up NOT measured)
cpu_seconds_lifetime and maxrss_bytes: RUSAGE_SELF of the whole process (imports included), so utilisation mixes scopes - stated in every status
scheduler-accounted allocated time per job (qstat -xf), settled into the campaign ledger by the operator: the authoritative cost
resamples accepted per job and across jobs, counted from strict checkpoint records (the watch), cross-checked against timing rows
recovery: n_resumed, n_tail_repaired, n_damaged, the watermark, stop acknowledgments with their request id and boundary, per start
not_in_this_slice: coverage against any reference (no policy-matched reference bank exists; the historical omega 1 reference is sensitivity evidence only)
any change to B, the policy, the seeds or the budget after submission
live_evaluation: chpc/row19_watch.py every 2 hours while any reservation is live, run by R052 from the Mac: it pulls fresh evidence (a failed pull is an alarm, never a green), counts accepted records from validated checkpoints, applies the first-record allowance (original + 2 resamples at the stage-0 expectation), the stall limit, the HELD and failed-resample alarms and the stop-acknowledgment check; on any alarm nothing further is submitted until it is diagnosed and recorded in the ledger row; a stop is requested through the campaign STOP file and lands at the next record boundary (the resample in flight completes and is committed; nothing in flight is lost)
